title: Sharp Controlled-Effect Sets over Families of Candidate Valid Instrument Sets
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling=7.3 < 7.4, salvageable=false; math panel revision findings remain unresolved and the note is not independently verified.
gap_reasons: The inference claim is narrower than its headline practical flavor because root-n set estimation requires fixed K and fixed separation from every candidate-feasibility boundary; only coverage, through a potentially conservative full-table projection, is uniform at switching boundaries.

The polynomial-time claim is polynomial in the explicitly tabulated size N=2^K, not in K, and the deferred certificate-emitting implementation leaves the computational contribution without reproducible software or worked certificate output.
The fixed-factorial scope, conservative inference, and absence of a substantive application or implementation constrain the leading-journal paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a compact candidatewise compatibility program, a common-core connectedness argument, and rational certification. D0.5 rated the package subfield below the required field floor (7.3 versus 7.4) and found no bounded in-scope tier lift. Its math panel requested four revisions that were not completed, so the draft is archived as unverified research and needs a fresh soundness review before reuse.
tldr: For any predeclared finite family \(\mathscr G\) of candidate globally valid encouragement-coordinate sets, the compact outcome-conditioned order polytope exactly tests each candidate against one shared response law. Every feasible candidate interval contains the observable core \([L_{S_{\mathscr G}(p)},U_{S_{\mathscr G}(p)}]\), so the sharp averaged controlled-effect set is the connected envelope \([\min_A L_A,\max_A U_A]\), including unequal nonproduct randomization and the empty-family case. The at-least-\(m\) model is the principal corollary obtained with \(\mathscr G=\mathscr V_m\). Rational endpoint laws and Farkas refutations are polynomial in the explicitly tabulated factorial input and the family encoding, and simultaneous full-table projection gives finite-sample uniform coverage plus root-\(n\) set estimation away from feasibility boundaries.
gap: Published unknown-validity models permit disconnected effect sets, while published generalized-monotonicity results settle fixed-model average-effect endpoints but do not characterize the union over unknown global validity sets. Generic multi-marginal optimal transport characterizes extrema over a fixed class of couplings with known marginals, but it does not encode candidate validity subsets, factorial exclusion, or coordinatewise monotonicity through one shared response law. Existing response-state reductions preserve a finite latent program but can retain superpolynomially many signatures, and existing many-instrument falsification results do not give an exact shared-law formulation for this factorial model.
fill: The project derives an exact polynomial-size order-polytope formulation, proves its constructive completion to one response law, uses published fixed-model corner formulas only as conditional calibration inputs, produces rational primal and Farkas certificates, and proves that the candidate intervals share an observable common core. It thereby separates compatibility, which may fail jointly, from scalar effect geometry, which remains connected.
